title: Al-Mu'min, the Giver of Safety
hook: the Giver of Safety and faith

segments.voice: Yesterday, As-Salam, Peace itself, the name inside the greeting. Your line was peace is his name.

Who would you call at three in the morning? Not the funniest friend or the smartest one. The safe one: the one who wouldn't tell anyone, wouldn't make you feel stupid, would just pick up. Long before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ received any revelation, the people of Mecca had a nickname for him. They left their valuables with him when they traveled. They called him al-Amin, the trustworthy one, the safe one. Today's name comes from the same three letters, and you already know it as the word for a believer.
screen: `THE ONE YOU'D CALL AT 3AM.` → `AL-AMIN, THE TRUSTWORTHY.` → `THE SAME THREE LETTERS.`

segments.voice: The root is a-m-n, and it grows a whole family. Amn: safety, the absence of fear. Amanah: a trust, something left in your keeping. Iman: faith. Amin: trustworthy. And the word Muslims say after the Fatiha, amin, so be it. At the end of al-Hashr, after Peace, comes al-Mu'min. Pickthall translates it the Keeper of Faith, and scholars give the name two meanings that sit together. First, the one who grants safety. The Qur'an says in Surah Quraysh that the Lord of the House fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear. Safety from fear is His gift. Second, the one who confirms: who affirms the truth of His messengers and keeps faith with His promises. He never breaks trust. Now the surprise. Mu'min is also the everyday word for a believer, a person of faith. The same word names Allah and names the people who trust Him. And the Prophet tied the two together in a very practical way. Tirmidhi and Nasa'i record him saying: the mu'min is the one from whom people's lives and property are safe. Another hadith, in Bukhari: the Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe. So a believer, in this sense, isn't first someone who holds the right ideas. It's someone people feel safe around. The name tells you what the one you trust is like, and what the one who trusts is meant to become.
screen: `A-M-N — SAFETY, TRUST, FAITH, AMIN.` · `THE ONE WHO GRANTS SAFETY.` · `THE ONE WHO CONFIRMS AND KEEPS FAITH.` · `A BELIEVER PEOPLE FEEL SAFE AROUND.` · then, large: `THE ONE WHO MAKES SAFE.`

segments.voice: Remember a time you felt completely safe with someone, where you were and what they did or didn't do, and let the feeling come back into your body: the shoulders dropping, the breath getting longer. Stay there for a few breaths. Then think of one person who might not feel safe right now, at home, at work, in their own head, and what would make them feel even a little safer around you: a kept secret, a calm voice, showing up when you said you would.
Al-Mu'min. The Giver of Safety, who grants safety from fear and keeps faith; also the word for a believer. Today's word.
Your line: the one who makes safe. A kept secret is a small amanah. Rest well.

howItsDone: Muslims describe the believer, the mu'min, by how safe others are around them, and treat promises, secrets and anything left in their care as an amanah, a trust; al-Amin, the trustworthy, was the Prophet's nickname in Mecca.

chat.meaning: Al-Mu'min, from a-m-n, is the one who grants safety from fear and keeps faith. Mu'min also names a believer.
